newsitem.title: UK: Britain rules out tough sanctions on Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Britain rules out tough sanctions on Nigeria.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday again ruled out harsh economic sanctions as a way of persuading Nigeria's military government to restore democracy in the populous oil-rich west African state.

Speaking during a brief parliamentary debate, junior Foreign Office minister Liam Fox reiterated Britain's stance that calls for an oil embargo, an assets freeze and a severing of trade ties were impractical.

"In our view these would require a United Nations Security Council resolution to be effective. An oil embargo would also have to be implemented through a naval blockade, and we judge these to be in practice unachievable at present," Fox said.
He said the government had also repeatedly made clear that Britain would not back a ban on air links unless all its European Union and Commonwealth partners did the same.

Nigerian military ruler Soni Abacha has remained defiant in the face of Commonwealth pressure, deftly exploiting splits within the group and refusing to bring forward plans to restore civil rule before 1998.
Nigeria was suspended from the 53-nation grouping of Britain and its former colonies in November last year after it defied world opinion by hanging nine activists, including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa.
Saro-Wiwa and his colleagues, campaigners for minority rights for the Ogoni tribe, had been found guilty of inciting the murder of four pro-government chiefs.
Fox said Nigeria illustrated the difficulty of striking the right balance when employing sanctions for political ends.

"Our aim is to identify carefully targetted measures that will be effective and send a clear signal of concern to the regime without wrecking the Nigerian economy and imposing hardship on its 100 million people any more than is required to achieve our political objectives," he said.

Fox was reporting on the visit to Nigeria last month of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG), which was given the task of investigating the situation in Nigeria and recommending how best to put it back on the path to democracy.
A demand by Canada last April for tough action was countered by calls from other CMAG members for continued dialogue and in the end the group held off imposing sanctions already agreed on.
Fox said it was too early to say what recommendations CMAG would make to the October 1997 summit of Commonwealth leaders in Edinburgh, Scotland.
